question: Among users who have obtained the “Teacher” badge, identify the user with the highest reputation. Count how many posts owned by this user have an above-average view count and have received at least 2 votes, and return this count as a single total value.

prediction.sql:
WITH teacher_users AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT u.XCL_052 AS user_id, u.XCL_053 AS reputation
    FROM users u
    INNER JOIN badges b ON u.XCL_052 = b.XCL_002
    WHERE b.XCL_003 = 'Teacher'
),
top_user AS (
    SELECT user_id
    FROM teacher_users
    ORDER BY reputation DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
avg_views AS (
    SELECT AVG(XCL_030) AS avg_view_count
    FROM posts
),
post_votes AS (
    SELECT v.XCL_067 AS post_id, COUNT(v.XCL_066) AS vote_count
    FROM votes v
    GROUP BY v.XCL_067
)
SELECT COUNT(p.XCL_026) AS total_count
FROM posts p
INNER JOIN top_user tu ON p.XCL_033 = tu.user_id
INNER JOIN avg_views av ON p.XCL_030 > av.avg_view_count
INNER JOIN post_votes pv ON p.XCL_026 = pv.post_id
WHERE pv.vote_count >= 2

WITH teacher_users AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT u.XCL_052 AS user_id, u.XCL_053 AS reputation
    FROM users u
    INNER JOIN badges b ON u.XCL_052 = b.XCL_002
    WHERE b.XCL_003 = 'Teacher'
),
top_user AS (
    SELECT user_id
    FROM teacher_users
    ORDER BY reputation DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
avg_views AS (
    SELECT AVG(XCL_030) AS avg_view_count
    FROM posts
),
post_votes AS (
    SELECT v.XCL_067 AS post_id, COUNT(v.XCL_066) AS vote_count
    FROM votes v
    GROUP BY v.XCL_067
)
SELECT COUNT(p.XCL_026) AS total_count
FROM posts p
INNER JOIN top_user tu ON p.XCL_033 = tu.user_id
INNER JOIN avg_views av ON p.XCL_030 > av.avg_view_count
INNER JOIN post_votes pv ON p.XCL_026 = pv.post_id
WHERE pv.vote_count >= 2

    SELECT DISTINCT u.XCL_052 AS user_id, u.XCL_053 AS reputation
    FROM users u
    INNER JOIN badges b ON u.XCL_052 = b.XCL_002
    WHERE b.XCL_003 = 'Teacher'
),
top_user AS (
    SELECT user_id
    FROM teacher_users
    ORDER BY reputation DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
avg_views AS (
    SELECT AVG(XCL_030) AS avg_view_count
    FROM posts
),
post_votes AS (
    SELECT v.XCL_067 AS post_id, COUNT(v.XCL_066) AS vote_count
    FROM votes v
    GROUP BY v.XCL_067
)
SELECT COUNT(p.XCL_026) AS total_count
FROM posts p
INNER JOIN top_user tu ON p.XCL_033 = tu.user_id
INNER JOIN avg_views av ON p.XCL_030 > av.avg_view_count
INNER JOIN post_votes pv ON p.XCL_026 = pv.post_id
WHERE pv.vote_count >= 2

scope_review.reason: The submitted SQL was semantically correct but timed out due to a full scan of the large votes table in the post_votes CTE. The fix removes the unnecessary join to posts in the post_votes CTE (since votes.XCL_067 is the post_id and we only need the count per post), which allows SQLite to use an index on votes.XCL_067 if available, or at least scan only the votes table once. The logic remains identical: find the top-reputation Teacher badge user, compute the average view count across all posts, count votes per post, and then count posts owned by that user that have above-average views and at least 2 votes.
checks: Teacher badge eligibility: Correctly uses badges.XCL_003 = 'Teacher' joined to users via badges.XCL_002 = users.XCL_052. Historical evidence (program::148488e4410942e545a90761) confirms this join and filter.
Highest reputation: Correctly orders teacher_users by users.XCL_053 DESC and takes LIMIT 1. Historical evidence (semantic::ea6ffad332089d865335a607) confirms XCL_053 is reputation.

Above-average view count: Correctly computes AVG(posts.XCL_030) over all posts and filters p.XCL_030 > avg_view_count. Historical evidence (recovered_column_hypotheses) confirms XCL_030 is view_count.

At least 2 votes: Correctly counts votes per post via COUNT(votes.XCL_066) GROUP BY votes.XCL_067 and filters vote_count >= 2. Historical evidence (recovered_column_hypotheses) confirms XCL_066 is vote_id and XCL_067 is post_id.
Post ownership: Correctly joins posts to top_user via posts.XCL_033 = top_user.user_id. Historical evidence (program::7eadfb9e01c68c79eaf135f9) confirms XCL_033 is owner_user_id.

Performance fix: The post_votes CTE now scans only the votes table instead of joining posts and votes, reducing the scan cost. The join to posts in the final SELECT ensures we only count posts owned by the top user.

base_solution_anchor.base_sql:
SELECT COUNT(p.XCL_026)
FROM posts p
WHERE p.XCL_033 = (
    SELECT u.XCL_052
    FROM users u
    INNER JOIN badges b ON u.XCL_052 = b.XCL_002
    WHERE b.XCL_003 = 'Teacher'
    ORDER BY u.XCL_053 DESC
    LIMIT 1
)
AND p.XCL_030 > (SELECT AVG(XCL_030) FROM posts)
AND p.XCL_031 >= 2
